args.name: Restorative sleep
args.function: Sleep safely at my current location when conditions permit, with an actual trial of whether sleep restores physical energy.
args.conditions: I am outdoors on ordinary soil at night, with no observed local hazards and other people nearby. My energy is 33.244 out of 40. My experience records 32 rounds of rest and zero recovered energy; I do not know why resting has not restored energy.
args.inputs: My own time and body; any required bedding or shelter must be identified rather than assumed available.
args.costs: Unknown; specify a feasible duration, prerequisites, and any exposure or interruption risks.
args.effects: Provide a feasible sleep method with observable recovery if physically supported, or explain unmet conditions. Do not assume recovery merely from requesting or learning it.

candidates.function: Draw a simple picture of something you see now by tracing short grooves with a finger in nearby soil, after a one-groove test of whether that patch keeps them.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds. test: surfaceRef ground (the only drawable surface) at x, y, a point at most 0.5 from you that you see now, not water, a body or any object; extent, the square patch side, 0.05-0.3 (default 0.3); method finger-groove (implement-groove and material-mark are refused as unavailable, naming what is missing); optional subjectRef. One round, 0.5 energy: one short test groove, which stays even if the soil fails. draw: subjectRef, an object you see now; strokes, 1-6, each 2-8 points as x, y offsets inside the patch, each at most extent long; two rounds, 0.5 energy each (one round for a single stroke), half the strokes per round, continuing; draw again resumes a pause. cancel: one round, no energy. All need light. Checks run before any charge.
candidates.effects: Forest floor and meadow ground (fine, yielding soil) keep a finger groove 0.02 wide and 0.01 deep unless waterlogged; rocky ground, a wet bank or waterlogged soil does not, and the test says why. No pigment or item is used: soil is pushed to the groove edges. A groove shows by its shaded floor: the ground tone darkened by 1 - 1/sqrt(1 + (2 depth / width)^2); contrast is the 0-1 colour distance, visible from 0.05. The grooves form one ground drawing nearby people see, with geometry, depth, colour, contrast, subject, strokes and status. Only performed strokes are recorded; completion means they were made, not that they look like the subject. Losing sight of the subject, reach, light or an unchanged patch pauses at no charge, as does an unworked round. No rain, trampling or erosion rule acts on ground marks here, so durability is untested. Nothing is refunded; no reward.

candidates.function: Inspect whole units of your own shelled food, such as hazelnuts, for visible defects, or shell a batch one unit at a time: press each on a clean hard support with your own blunt implement (or by hand where that works), then separate kernel and shell. Kernels are unverified, not certified food.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds. inspect: targetStack (your own unreserved, untreated item of a material with represented shell and kernel) and quantity (whole units, 1-5, default 1); one round, 0.2 energy per unit. shell: targetStack and quantity reserve that batch in a work record (workId); each unit then takes a press round and a separation round, 0.5 energy each; a press that only cracks the shell adds a round. Press with implementRef (your own whole, hard, sound inedible piece) on supportRef (a solid unreserved inedible object in reach, not a plant or animal, with no loose item on it, or another such own piece on firm ground where you stand), or by hand with neither. shell continues round by round until the batch is done; shell again (or with workId) resumes a pause. cancel: one round, no energy. All need light. Checks run before any charge; a failed recheck pauses open work at no charge.
candidates.effects: Inspection records ripeness, shell state, deterioration and spoilage by eye (mould and infestation are not represented); spoiled or visibly deteriorated units are set aside as a rejected item and not shelled. Strength is hardness / 10; a press passes the lower of implement and support strength x (1 - flexibility), a bare hand 0.1 / unit mass^(2/3). At or below the shell strength the shell holds: an unmet-prerequisite result that pauses the work, and that method is refused for it. Above it damage (load - strength) / strength accumulates: below 1 cracked, at 1 split open. Separation makes a kernel item and a shell item whose quantities are their mass shares and sum to the unit; the kernel carries all of its food value and toxicity, origin, age and decay, is inspected by eye and is an unverified shelled specimen or a rejected item, never certified food; a 0.4 item is less than the whole unit eat takes. Nothing is washed, heated or made safe. Unworked rounds pause; cancel returns reserved units as they now are; death drops them. Nothing is refunded; no reward.
